title: Kotosoupa Avgolemono
subtitle: Greek chicken and rice soup finished with lemon and egg
excerpt: A whole chicken simmered until the broth is deep and golden, then finished with egg beaten with lemon juice to give the soup a creamy, silky texture. Simple, restorative and very good.
sourceNotes: Kotosoupa kreas: Greek chicken soup, classically finished with avgolemono egg and lemon liaison.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the chicken and make the broth a day ahead. Add the rice and avgolemono just before serving.

content.text: Kotosoupa is a slow-simmered Greek chicken soup, finished with avgolemono, a mixture of beaten egg and lemon that thickens the broth without curdling. The soup must not boil once the egg goes in. Pull it off the heat the moment you see steam rising after adding the liaison.
Place the chicken in a large stockpot. Cover with cold water by about 5cm. Add the onion, carrots, celery, bay leaves, peppercorns and salt. Bring to the boil.
Skim off any foam that rises to the surface. Reduce the heat to a gentle simmer. Cover partially and cook for 75 minutes.
Lift the chicken out and set it aside to cool slightly. Strain the broth through a sieve into a clean pot. Discard the vegetables.
Bring the broth back to a simmer. Add the rice and cook for 18 minutes until tender.
Pull the chicken meat from the bones in large pieces. Discard the skin and bones. Add the meat back to the soup.
Beat the eggs and lemon juice together in a bowl. Ladle a cup of hot broth slowly into the egg mixture, whisking constantly to temper it. Pour this back into the soup.
Stir gently over a very low heat for 2 minutes. Do not boil. The soup should be thick and slightly creamy. Taste and add more salt or lemon if needed.

items.symptom: The egg mixture curdled when added to the soup.
items.cause: The soup was too hot, or the egg was not tempered slowly enough.
items.fix: Add the hot broth to the egg very slowly, whisking the whole time. The soup must not be boiling when the egg goes in.

items.cause: The chicken boiled rather than simmered, or foam was not skimmed.
items.fix: Keep the heat at the lowest simmer. Skim diligently in the first 10 minutes.

items.symptom: The soup is not thick enough after the egg.
items.cause: Too few eggs were used, or the soup simmered too briefly after adding the avgolemono.
items.fix: Stir over a gentle heat for a full 2 to 3 minutes. The egg needs time to thicken the broth.
